blocks.content: The Environment Protection Act of 1986 serves as an umbrella legislation designed to provide a framework for central and state coordination in environmental protection.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Stockholm Conference of 1972 established the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and laid global environmental governance foundations.
India enacted the Environment Protection Act (EPA) in 1986 under Article 253 as umbrella legislation following the Bhopal Gas Tragedy.
The 1992 Rio Earth Summit birthed key conventions including UNFCCC, Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), and UNCCD.
Constitutional provisions Article 48A (DPSP) and Article 51A(g) (Fundamental Duty) mandate environmental protection in India.
The National Green Tribunal (NGT) Act, 2010 provides statutory power for expeditious disposal of environmental disputes.

MoEFCC, CPCB, SPCB, National Green Tribunal (NGT)

items: Article 253 empowers Parliament to enact national laws to give effect to international treaties and agreements.
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added Article 48A (State duty) and Article 51A(g) (Fundamental Duty) for environmental protection.
NGT has jurisdiction over civil cases involving substantial questions relating to the environment under key statutes including EPA 1986.
